newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends up on rise expectations.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends up on rise expectations.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended up on Monday due to expectations of further rises despite last Friday's losses on the London Metal Exchange, traders said.
The most active April 1997 contract ended at 21,760 yuan ($2,622) per tonne, rising 230 yuan. It opened at an intra-day low of 21,450 and hit a high of 21,770.
January rose 350 to 21,200, February 240 to 21,250, March 190 to 21,450, May 200 to 21,860, June 120 to 21,820 and July 100 to 21,900. The first traded August ended at 21,850.
Combined volume fell to 45,890 tonnes from 76,770.
Copper opened mixed at intra-day lows, but follow-up buying pushed all the contracts up to close at or near their intra-day highs.
Traders said optimistic expectations and good technical charts supported confidence of many long position holders in Shanghai.
"Many investors expect domestic fundamentals to improve later this year," one trader said. "And Friday's falls in LME stockpiles helped to boost market sentiment a little."
"Technical charts also indicate further rises in the short term," he added.
